0013 — Detector maturity levels and the evidence to move between them

Status: accepted

Problem

Epics for Rust (#46), .NET (#48), and Java and Kotlin (#49) list "detector maturity is at least beta" and "precision on the independent corpus is at least 0.95" as exit criteria, but nothing says what beta is or how much evidence earns it. The only machine-readable signal is stable in benchmarks/thresholds.json, which says whether the precision floor is enforced and not why. Three consequences:

  • Epics were closed with their criteria unmet, and the reason lived only in a comment.
  • The documentation says Supported and Experimental; the roadmap says beta; the thresholds file says stable.
  • Four detectors are enforced today (github-actions, nodejs, npm, python) on evidence that differs by an order of magnitude, and nothing records that.

Decision

1. Three levels, one vocabulary

Level Shown in the docs as What it promises users Precision floor in CI
experimental Experimental It runs and is usable. Findings, rule ids, and unclassified output may change between releases without notice. Scored and reported, never fails the run.
beta Beta Findings were checked against ground truth on enough repositories to measure them. A change to a rule id, a finding id, or a documented declaration form is listed in the changelog. Enforced (0.95).
stable Supported The same as beta, on a larger and more varied corpus, and part of the documented product contract. Enforced (0.95).

Supported in the docs is the word for stable. The thresholds file gains a level field with these three values; stable: true means level is beta or stable (the floor is enforced), and a test keeps the two in step.

2. Evidence required, per detector

A detector is named by the first segment of its rule ids. "Repositories with findings" counts corpus repositories that have at least one expected finding of that detector; "zero-finding repositories" counts corpus repositories of the detector's ecosystem with no expected findings at all.

experimental beta stable
Conformance suite passes on positive, negative, zero, and malformed fixtures yes yes yes
Repositories with findings 1 8 20
Expected findings (all with a groundTruthSource) 1 15 60
Zero-finding repositories 1 2 4
Precision on the whole corpus reported at least 0.95 at least 0.95
Recall on the whole corpus reported at least 0.80 at least 0.90
Selection any at least half of the repositories chosen blind at least two thirds chosen blind
A full corpus run on the current main, recorded in the thresholds file no within 30 days within 30 days
A detector page in docs/detectors/ stating what is and is not judged yes yes yes

Blind means the repository was chosen by a rule fixed before running Offing on it (for example the first results of a public search query, minus forks and archives), not because it is known to contain a finding. A repository picked because it had a migration commit is useful ground truth but is a targeted pick, and the corpus must say which is which: each corpus entry gains selection: "targeted" | "blind".

Independent ground truth is one of the kinds the corpus already records: a maintainer's own migration commit, an upstream changelog or release note, a vendor lifecycle page, or a reviewer's written check of the cited line. It is never Offing's own output.

3. Who decides, and where it is recorded

A promotion is a pull request that changes level in benchmarks/thresholds.json and records, next to it, the corpus run the claim rests on (date, commit, per-detector precision, recall, and the counts above). The maintainer merges it. A comment on an epic is not a record. An epic's exit criterion "maturity is at least X" is met only when the thresholds file says so.

A demotion is the same pull request in reverse and is also required when a full run shows precision or recall below the floor and it is not fixed within 30 days.

4. Epic exit criteria

Exit criteria that mention maturity should say "at the level in the thresholds file", not a fixed word. An epic whose work is finished but whose detector has not earned the next level is closed with a follow-up issue naming the missing evidence, as for #727 and #736.

Applying it to today's detectors

Counts are from benchmarks/public-repositories/ on 2026-10-19 (90 repositories). Precision and recall are from the full run recorded in benchmarks/thresholds.json (lastFullRun): 85 repositories on commit b19a781, 336 reported findings, 336 true positives, 0 false positives, 0 false negatives.

Detector Level today Repositories with findings Expected findings Zero-finding repositories Meets
github-actions stable 33 205 2 beta (stable needs 4 zero-finding repositories)
nodejs stable 12 40 8 beta (stable needs 20 repositories and 60 findings)
python stable 17 19 2 beta (stable needs 20 repositories, 60 findings, 4 zero)
npm stable 8 10 8 experimental (beta needs 15 findings)
container experimental 6 16 1 experimental (beta needs 8 repositories and 2 zero)
.NET experimental 5 23 1 experimental (beta needs 8 repositories and 2 zero)
Go experimental 4 7 1 experimental
Java and Kotlin experimental 4 6 1 experimental
Kubernetes experimental 4 9 1 experimental
Rust experimental 4 5 1 experimental

Every detector scored precision 1 and recall 1 in that run, so the precision and recall rows of the table are met by all ten detectors and do not separate them. That is a weaker statement than it sounds: the expected findings were written by reviewing the files at each pinned commit, and the corpus was grown until it matched, so 1.0 shows that nothing regressed, not that the detectors generalize. Only blind-selected repositories and more of them can show that, which is why the evidence table counts repositories and selection and not just the score.

Selection (blind or targeted) is not recorded yet, so the selection row cannot be checked for any detector; recording it is part of this change.

The four detectors that predate this decision keep their current Supported label as a grandfathered state, listed by name in the test that enforces the table. The record states plainly that none of them reaches stable on the numbers above and that npm is below beta on expected findings. Growing the corpus (#141 and #142) is how they earn the label, not a reason to hide the gap.

Alternatives rejected

  • Keep stable as a boolean. It cannot tell a detector with 201 expected findings from one with 10.
  • Fixed numbers inside the epics. They drift and are checked by nobody; the thresholds file is checked by CI.
  • Require recall only for stable. A detector that misses half of what is there is not a beta promise.

Consequences

  • benchmarks/thresholds.json gains level and a run record; a test checks that level agrees with stable, with the Status column of docs/COMPATIBILITY.md, and that each beta and stable detector meets the counts above (the grandfathered ones are named).
  • The corpus schema gains an optional selection field. Adding it to the existing 85 entries is a separate change; until then blind-selection is reported as unknown.
  • No detector changes level in this record. Promotions follow, one pull request each, with their corpus run.
  • Recall becomes a measured number per detector; today only precision is computed.

Update 2026-10-19: .NET promoted to beta (#736)

The .NET corpus grew from six repositories to eighteen: six targeted and twelve chosen blind by the rule in Validation. Counts for the dotnet detector on 2026-10-19: nine repositories with findings, 84 expected findings, nine zero-finding repositories, and twelve of eighteen repositories blind, which meets every row of the beta column. The full run recorded in benchmarks/thresholds.json reported precision 1 and recall 1 for dotnet; recall was also checked by hand over the blind repositories (see .NET), which found one gap before the promotion (no rule for the 1.x, 2.x, and 3.0 lines) and closed it. The two .NET repositories with workflow findings also raise GitHub Actions to 35 repositories with findings and 211 expected findings; the table above is the 90-repository snapshot and is left as written. The selection row is now checked by the test for any detector that records selection; entries without it count as not blind.

Update 2026-10-21: Serverless runtimes promoted to beta

The Serverless corpus grew to ten repositories: five targeted and five chosen blind by the rule in Validation. Counts for the serverless detector on 2026-10-21: nine repositories with findings (including the existing trpc/trpc Node.js corpus pin), twenty expected findings, two zero-finding repositories, and five of ten Serverless-ecosystem repositories blind, which meets every row of the beta column. The detector page is Serverless runtimes. The full run recorded with this promotion reports precision and recall for serverless in benchmarks/thresholds.json.

Update 2026-10-21: Swift promoted to beta

The Swift corpus grew from six repositories to thirteen: six targeted and seven chosen blind by the rule in Validation. Counts for the swift detector on 2026-10-21: ten repositories with findings, fifteen expected findings, two zero-finding repositories, and seven of thirteen Swift repositories blind, which meets every row of the beta column. The detector page is Swift. The full run recorded with this promotion reports precision and recall for swift in benchmarks/thresholds.json. Three of the blind repositories also carry GitHub Actions and Ruby findings, which are recorded on those pins and are not Swift findings.

Update 2026-10-23: Java and Kotlin promoted to beta (#727)

The Java corpus grew from five repositories to seventeen: five targeted and twelve chosen blind by the rule in Validation. Counts for the java detector on 2026-10-23: thirteen repositories with findings, 66 expected findings, three zero-finding repositories, and twelve of seventeen Java-ecosystem repositories blind, which meets every row of the beta column. Recall was checked by hand over the blind repositories; the one JDK declaration the detector does not report is inside a Maven profile, which the detector page lists as not judged. The detector page is Java and Kotlin. Still not covered by the corpus: .java-version, .sdkmanrc, .tool-versions, Groovy build.gradle, and the slf4j relocation; the fixtures cover them.

Update 2026-10-23: Kubernetes APIs promoted to beta (#728)

The Kubernetes corpus grew from five repositories to seventeen: five targeted and twelve chosen blind by the rule in Validation. Counts for the kubernetes detector on 2026-10-23: ten repositories with findings, 67 expected findings, two zero-finding repositories, and twelve of seventeen Kubernetes-ecosystem repositories blind, which meets every row of the beta column. Recall was checked by hand over the blind repositories; every removed apiVersion the detector does not report is a form the detector page lists as not judged (kind: List items, references below the top level, and skipped test directories). The detector page is Kubernetes APIs. Still not covered by the corpus: Chart.yaml kubeVersion, kustomize patch targets, and a template guarded by .Capabilities; the fixtures cover them. The 45 rules the kubernetes-1 importer drafts remain unreviewed and are not part of this promotion.

Update 2026-10-23: recall floors and recorded selection (#740)

Every corpus entry now records selection: the 84 entries that predate the field were chosen from reviewed migration commits or known findings and record targeted. The corpus test fails for an entry without it. A full corpus run enforces the recall floors of the table above (0.80 for beta, 0.90 for stable) next to the precision floor and refuses to record a run below either. Still open under #740: a held-out, blind-selected set with ground truth written before the scan, and the grandfathered detectors.

Update 2026-10-23 (issue #740)

The corpus has 455 repositories, 155 of them added blind in this pass, and github-actions, nodejs, npm, and python each meet stable on the counted evidence, so no detector is grandfathered. A separate held-out set (benchmarks/held-out-repositories.json) has ground truth committed before the scan; its first result (recall 0.75, precision 0.96 on its scope) is in VALIDATION.md. The full run is recorded twice a month by the record job in .github/workflows/corpus.yml.

Update 2026-11-07: Java and Kotlin, and Scala and sbt, promoted to stable (#1896)

The Java corpus grew from seventeen repositories to twenty-five: five targeted and twenty chosen blind (twelve from the 2026-10-23 beta rule, eight from the 2026-11-07 stable-expansion rule in Validation). Counts for the java detector on 2026-11-07: twenty-one repositories with findings, 71 expected findings, four zero-finding repositories, and twenty of twenty-five repositories blind, which meets every row of the stable column. Offline validate on the Java bucket reported precision 1 and recall 1 for java.

The Scala corpus was created from scratch the same day: eighty repositories chosen blind by the rule in Validation. Counts for the scala detector on 2026-11-07: fifty-one repositories with findings, 77 expected findings, twelve zero-finding repositories, and all eighty repositories blind, which meets every row of the stable column. Offline validate on the Scala bucket reported precision 1 and recall 1 for scala. Scala 2.12 / 2.13 / 3.3 pins are included as controls that the detector intentionally does not judge.
